newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast lt. crudes rise, but heavies ease.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast lt. crudes rise, but heavies ease.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices rose Friday with WTI/Cushing markets, while heavies continued to ease as another California major oil company cut their buying price for heavy grade overnight, brokers said..
Texaco cut their bids 50 cents a barrel to $15.50, bringing the price average for major California heavy crudes to $15.63 a barrel.

Heavy crudes sold for $1.00 to $3.00 under the average, with perceptions of further weakness after traders familiar with Tosco's Avon refinery said Friday a damaged unit would stay shut longer than expected, backing crude into markets.
Outright prices for heavies stood $12.63/14.73 a barrel after Texaco cut its Kern River buying price.

BP America, the dominant seller of Alaska North Slope crude, declined to give an offer price Friday, with buyers claiming the company was watching to see if refiners could switch more of their slates over to cheaper heavy crude.
